sentences.span: US Info Tech long/short ratio now stands at 1.5 (vs. YTD peak of 2.14 seen in early June), the lowest level on our record (since 2016).
sentences.why: Goldman's Armbrust note gives the 1.5 ratio and 'lowest level on record since 2016' verbatim; the companion Goldman-sourced piece (27341__shorting-the-rip...) independently states 'leaves hedge funds more than 20 points underweight tech vs. the S&P, per Goldman's chart', confirming the second clause.

sentences.span: The entire increase came from the market going up and from covering index hedges; nobody actually bought anything. Net is still in the 2nd percentile of the past five years.
sentences.why: Exact match on mechanism (market up + covering, not buying) and the '2nd percentile of the past five years' figure for net leverage.

sentences.span: Retail was more engaged, buying an estimated ~$25B over the past week through Thursday... retail net bought $1.6B of Nvidia (NVDA) on Thursday, nearly 10x the demand of the next-most-bought single name
sentences.why: All three figures (~$25B weekly retail, $1.6B NVDA Thursday, nearly 10x next-most-bought) appear verbatim in the Morgan Stanley (Savone) note, attributed to MS's QDS models.

sentences.span: while the bond market, which hadn't priced any of it, had to do all the work... the question for next week is whether the bond market's verdict eventually reaches stocks
sentences.why: Opinion-shaped sentence; the source explicitly frames bonds and stocks as reacting differently to the week's news, with the piece stating 'We side with the bond market' against the equity market's calmer read -- supports 'priced something else entirely' as a compressed paraphrase of a documented stance.

sentences.span: We continue to prefer hyperscalers to the high-beta AI players, favoring balance-sheet strength and free-cash-flow durability.
sentences.why: Verbatim JPMorgan (confirmed via meta.json source field and 'J P M O R G A N' header) statement of preference for hyperscalers over high-beta AI names.

sentences.span: Jensen Huang has resigned, effective immediately, with CFO Colette Kress taking over as interim CEO (while keeping the CFO job)
sentences.why: Near-verbatim match, corroborated across multiple sources (27254, 27247, 27252, 27343) all describing resignation effective immediately and Kress as interim CEO retaining the CFO role.

sentences.span: Kress, as both interim CEO and CFO, presents Q3 results on Nov 17... Somebody will ask her about the $500 billion.
sentences.why: Matches the setup exactly: Kress presenting on the earnings call, with the open question being whether she stands behind the $500bn financing platform.

sentences.span: AI-related high yield spreads have blown out to roughly 425bp against about 265bp for non-AI BB/B paper... Wheeler also flagged the trapdoor... investment grade tenant wraps only become effective on completion
sentences.why: Figures (425bp vs 265bp), the no-new-deals-since-September detail, and the IG tenant guarantee mechanic all match Goldman's Miriam Wheeler commentary verbatim.

sentences.span: we have seen the all-time widest print on AAAs (200)... We believe this weakness is primarily driven by technical factors, rather than fundamental concerns over the thematic backdrop.
sentences.why: Morgan Stanley note gives the all-time-wide 200bp AAA print and explicitly frames it as a technical/supply issue rather than a thematic verdict.

sentences.span: We close our underweight on HQ hyperscalers, and add selectively at the long-end.
sentences.why: Morgan Stanley verbatim; 'HQ hyperscalers' = high-quality hyperscaler credit.

sentences.span: P/E multiples contracted by about 37 log points overall... for these stocks, the de-rating accounts for more than the entire price decline... 30 Sep to cut-off... 5 Nov 2026 close for all others
sentences.why: Morgan Stanley's decomposition exhibit uses the exact 30 Sep to 5 Nov window and finds valuation (de-rating) accounts for more than the entire price decline, i.e. almost entirely valuation-driven.

sentences.span: US and Europe moved from the middle of their ranges to the bottom quintile (median percentiles 17 and 13). Japan de-rated most, from the 82nd to the 28th percentile, even though every Japanese member saw flat or higher FY2 estimates... 7 of its 26 members (27%) saw FY2 consensus cut by more than 0.5%
sentences.why: The quintile figures and Japan's 82nd-to-28th percentile move are correct, but 'no member seeing lower estimates' misattributes a Japan-specific fact (every Japanese member saw flat/higher FY2 estimates) to the whole set: the same source states 27% of Asia/EM members did see FY2 estimates cut over the period, so the generalized 'no member' claim is false.

sentences.span: We expect Eurozone earnings to grow 15% next year and remain positive on the region's equities.
sentences.why: UBS verbatim for the earnings growth/stance clause; Morgan Stanley's 'Raise MSCI Europe target to 3030 (+15% upside)' (27326) confirms the second clause.

sentences.span: even France's CAC-40 was outperforming our basket of AI-winners over the last 12mths (chart 1), and that European banks have now outperformed the mighty 'Mag7' over 1yr, 2yrs, 3yrs, 4yrs & 5yrs
sentences.why: Verbatim match from Goldman's Peter Wilson weekly note for both comparisons.

sentences.span: Bitcoin is once again trading below Strategy's average purchase price... Funding turned negative on Binance, OKX and Bybit on November 13. That's an important shift: the market is no longer just liquidating longs; traders are increasingly paying to be short.
sentences.why: Both clauses match verbatim, including the exact three exchanges and date.
